the_trade_off_made: We favored impact and legal risk over pure fairness and monetary considerations, meaning we may delay less urgent but still important fairness concerns, costing us a slower response to the disgruntled dashboard user.
hardest_call: Choosing whether the security incident (NEW-00004) or the GDPR request (NEW-00002) should be third was hardest, as both have strong arguments; we placed the security incident higher due to the policy lift, but the legal deadline could also justify a higher rank.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Impact on users and business continuity varied widely and directly reflects the urgency of the problem.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: It can undervalue legal deadlines or policy lifts that are not captured by raw damage numbers.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Remaining SLA time influences how quickly we must act, especially for near‑deadline tickets.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: Deadlines may be generous for low‑impact issues, causing them to outrank more critical technical failures.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: Ensures equal treatment of all customers regardless of payment, but is less decisive when impact differs sharply.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: May promote lower‑impact tickets over higher‑impact ones.

how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.why_it_ranks_here: All tickets are from free plans, so monetary weighting adds little useful signal.
how_it_ranked_the_four_ways.what_it_gets_wrong: Ignores the fact that paying customers might deserve faster service, but here it would mislead.

why_the_winner_beat_the_runner_up: Damage ranking outranked deadline because the sheer number of affected users and blocked work outweighed the remaining SLA time for the next ticket.

reasons_before_correction.NEW-00005: Dashboard showing stale data impacts a small set of users and is low priority after higher‑impact issues.
